sn52.8:1.1: _Salaḷa_ was the awakening tree of the Buddha Paduma ([tha-ap179:1.2]()), which suggests it was a large tree. It is sometimes identified with frankincense (_sallakī_, Sanskrit _śallakī_, *Boswellia serrata*), but seems to me unlikely. Frankincense thrives in arid highlands quite distant from the rich riverlands of Sāvatthī, and is a straggly tree unsuited to construction (although the hut could simply be near a frankincense). The flowers or garlands of _salaḷa_ are, in poetry, abundant (eg. [ja511:27.3](), [tha-ap209](), [tha-ap556:3.3)), but the frankincense flower is small and a poor candidate for garlands. [mn93:11.6]() and [mn96:16.3]() speak of the fire of the _salaḷa_, but no Pali reference, so far as I know, speaks of the most characteristic feature of frankincense, its aromatic gum used for incense. Sometimes the variant readings suggest a confusion with the pine tree _sarala_ (*Pinus roxburghii*, [sn56.32:2.2]()), but that of course has no flowers.
